purpose: Source-backed historical reports of related institutional themes and public worker-rights, disability and policy resources in the Peninsula and Silicon Valley. Not a list of workers or associates to receive individual allegations.
scope_notes: Different legal entities and employment/education/healthcare jurisdictions are distinguished. Public reports do not establish a connected pattern, causation, or culpability in the user's case.

Preserve primary reporting, worker/union claims, organizational responses, formal dockets, contract outcomes and case dispositions as different evidence types. Open charges are allegations, not findings.

No private or public-facing personal survivor/worker contact details, names, lists of signatories, union member directories or communications channels collected. References identify the reporting organization or public docket. Group association does not establish shared experience.

Use competent medical/civil-rights authorities for individual allegations. Worker organizations and regional civic groups may supply relevant general policy or worker-rights resources through their public channels; membership and endorsements are not inferred.
No attempt to map Stanford's unrelated corporate, investor, alumni, family or personal influence network. Publicly documented employment and representation relationships are used for scope only.
